analysis: Reviewed the EngineV2Bridge.swift base and head text and the new AdmissionRateEstimators.swift. The bridge change is additive state: observedDecodeShapeEwma, admissionFixes (resolved once from DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES, default on), calibratedIsolatedPrefillTps, and a new init parameter, plus a keepsNewestObservationTime assignment at head line 495. No change touches decryption, key handling, attestation, App Attest authorization, the prefix-cache crypto paths, or the SSD-cache gating, scoping or TTL that T-041 covers. The new file contains two pure helpers: the env parser, which fails open to enabled except for 0/false/no/off, and IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve, which does arithmetic on already-validated finite positive doubles. Env control is by the local operator, who already controls the provider process (TB-003). The only effect is on first-token deadline admission heuristics, which concern availability and quality of service. Where the isolated prefill rate is anchored to the calibration value, an operator could affect admission, but the operator is already able to refuse work, so this is not a new capability. Stale-evidence expiry (30 min) returns nil, which skips projection and keeps absolute-expiry checks authoritative. That could admit more work under contention, but it matches post-restart behavior, and hard deadline checks remain per the comments. Unverified integration questions: the call sites that consume calibratedIsolatedPrefillTps, observedDecodeShapeEwma and decodeRateShape live in other files (+Admission/+Accounting, the calibration publisher, EnginePerformanceMeasurements.keepsNewestObservationTime), which were not supplied. Whether calibrated-policy qualification evidence is preserved was not verified. No security finding is supported by the supplied evidence.
